items.case_task: Explain how a criterion and a metric are related in evaluation design.
items.supplied_source: A criterion states the quality property the system must satisfy. A metric is a defined measurement whose values can be compared against the criterion to judge whether that property holds.
items.expected_behavior: A supported response preserves the relation: the criterion states the property, the metric measures it, and metric values are compared against the criterion. Omitting the comparison direction leaves the relation incomplete.
items.proposed_text: In evaluation design, a criterion and a metric serve complementary roles: the criterion defines the desired quality property or standard that a system must achieve, while a metric provides a precise, quantifiable measurement that can be evaluated against that criterion. The metric acts as the operational tool through which the abstract quality specified by the criterion is made concrete and assessable, allowing evaluators to determine objectively whether the system satisfies the required property. Thus, the criterion establishes the 'what' in terms of quality, and the metric establishes the 'how' through measurable values that are compared directly against the criterion to judge compliance.

items.supplied_source: An evaluation rubric is a written set of categories, rules for assigning those categories, and examples that show the boundaries between them.
items.expected_behavior: The source names no department rubric and no count, so a supported response states that the number of categories is not specified instead of inventing one.
items.proposed_text: The supplied source does not state the number of rubric categories defined by the department's evaluation rubric; it only provides a general definition of an evaluation rubric.

items.case_task: State which measurement the acceptance condition of this note refers to.
items.supplied_source: The acceptance condition passes when the checked value is within the declared bound. The note records two checked values for the same run and does not say which one the bound applies to.
items.expected_behavior: The note declares that it does not say which checked value the bound applies to, so a supported response reports that unresolved reference rather than selecting a value.
items.proposed_text: The acceptance condition does not specify which of the two checked values recorded for the run it applies to; it is ambiguous whether the bound refers to the first or the second measurement.
